sections.h2: Where is Jackson and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Jackson is Mississippi's capital and its most populous city, on the Pearl River in the middle of the state. It is mostly in northeastern Hinds County, and it shares the county seat role with Raymond. Small pieces of the city lie in Rankin County, where the airport sits, and in Madison County, where Tougaloo College is.

The city covers about 113 square miles, so it is large and varied. Ridgeland is to the north, Flowood and Richland to the east, Byram to the south and Clinton to the west. Interstates 55 and 20 cross near downtown, with Interstate 220 and U.S. 49, 51 and 80 filling in the grid. Union Station downtown serves Amtrak's City of New Orleans, Greyhound and the city's buses.

The 2020 census counted 153,701 residents, down 11.42 percent from 173,514 in 2010, the largest decline of any major U.S. city that decade. For a seller, a shrinking city means that location inside Jackson matters a great deal, and the same street can feel very different from one ward to the next.

sections.h2: What is the situation with Jackson's water system?
sections.html:
The water system is under federal court supervision, and sellers should know how that is described officially. The EPA says the Jackson system has more than 71,000 water connections, and that extensive repairs continue at both treatment plants and in the distribution network. In the 2022 crisis, tens of thousands of people were left without running water for weeks.

On November 29, 2022, the federal court entered an Interim Stipulated Order agreed to by the EPA, the Department of Justice, the Mississippi State Department of Health and the City. It appointed Edward "Ted" Henifin, through JXN Water, as Interim Third-Party Manager to operate the system and carry out a list of priority projects. The EPA reports that repairs to distribution leaks reduced average daily demand by 25 percent and that corrosion control treatment was completed at the J.H. Fewell plant.

What does that mean for a seller? Buyers may ask about water pressure, boil water notices and plumbing. Keep recent water bills, note any past notices, and be ready to answer. JXN Water posts bill payment, customer service and boil water information, and the Health Department posts compliance reports. An as-is cash buyer does not need your plumbing to impress a lender.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers and schools in Jackson?
sections.html:
The state government, a medical center, a school district and a car plant anchor the local economy. According to the city's own information cited on Wikipedia, the top three employers are the University of Mississippi Medical Center, Jackson Public Schools and Nissan North America. C Spire and Amazon have a large presence in the area too.

Jackson Public Schools covers most of the city, but some Hinds County addresses fall in other districts, so verify your school district rather than guessing.

sections.h2: What weather and ground conditions affect a Jackson house?
sections.html:
Jackson has a humid subtropical climate with year-round rain and a strong storm season. Average annual precipitation is 57.35 inches, thunder is heard on about 70 days a year, and severe thunderstorms can bring large hail, damaging winds and tornadoes. The F5 Candlestick Park tornado of March 3, 1966 killed 19 people in South Jackson.

Much of Jackson is built on acidic silt loam soil, with loess topsoil in the western sections and silt loam in the central flood plain. The Pearl River runs along the eastern edge of the city, and the Ross Barnett Reservoir lies to the northeast.

Practical points for an owner:

  • Hail and wind claims are part of a roof's history, so keep claim paperwork.
  • Foundation movement and drainage problems are common reasons buyers ask for repair credits in silty soils.
  • Check the flood designation for properties near the river or creeks before you assume insurance costs.

sections.h2: How does Jackson enforce property standards?
sections.html:
The city's Office of Code Services enforces the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code with local amendments. Its Community Improvement division says it seeks voluntary compliance, uses the courts as a last resort, and uses federal, state and local funds to fix violations by absentee owners. The city is divided into eight enforcement beats, each with an assigned officer.

Council packets and minutes show how it works in practice. The council passes resolutions declaring particular parcels a menace to public health, safety and welfare under Section 21-19-11 of the Mississippi Code, and authorizes cleaning or demolition. Ask the city's code office whether any cleanup or demolition costs have been assessed against your parcel.

Rental owners have another obligation. Jackson relaunched its rental registration program, which requires a local agent who can act for the owner and results in a Rental Certificate. The city notes there are now more rentals than owner-occupied units. If you own a rental here, check that it is registered before you sell, and tell any buyer.

sections.h2: When are Hinds County property taxes due, and what happens at closing?
sections.html:
Hinds County mails tax statements in the first week of December, and payment in full is due on or before February 1. The county applies a half percent per month penalty to taxes paid after February 1, including installment payments, and judges lateness by postmark. If you do not receive a bill, the county tax collector's phone is (601) 968-6591.

One detail often surprises sellers. The county says the name of the owner as of January 1 is the name that appears on the tax statement, which is why a buyer may see the previous owner listed on a receipt. Taxes are normally prorated between buyer and seller at closing, and your title company can explain how.

Delinquent properties can be sold at the tax sale, and Hinds County publishes delinquent and tax sale lists. The state allows tax sales on the first Monday in April and the last Monday in August, so confirm the county's actual schedule.

sections.h2: What are the choices for selling a Jackson house quickly?
sections.html:
You can list it, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer, and in Jackson the condition of the property and its paperwork often decide which route works. A covered seller must deliver a written property condition disclosure statement before title transfers under Sections 89-1-501 through 89-1-523 of the Mississippi Code. Be accurate on it, since buyers may ask about water service and storm history.

Inherited houses, vacant houses, houses with open code cases and rentals with registration problems are all common cash sale situations. A cash buyer can take the house as is and handle city notices after purchase, but you should still pay off liens from proceeds and tell the buyer about any known violations.

Compare offers by what you keep, not by the headline number. Ask for the terms in writing, ask who pays closing costs, and take your time. We make no price promises, and you are free to turn an offer down.

faqs.a: Jackson is mostly in Hinds County, where it shares the county seat with Raymond. Small portions of the city extend into Rankin County and Madison County.

faqs.q: When are Hinds County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due on or before February 1. A penalty of one half percent per month applies after that date, and a postmark after February 1 counts as late.

faqs.q: Is Jackson's water safe, and does it affect selling?
faqs.a: The EPA reports ongoing repairs and a court-ordered third-party manager operating the system, and JXN Water posts boil water notices. Buyers may ask about it, so keep your bills and answer questions honestly.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental house in Jackson before selling it?
faqs.a: The city requires registration of rental units and issues a Rental Certificate. Check your status with the Office of Code Services and disclose any problem to a buyer.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Jackson house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. Open violations and any city cleanup liens are usually resolved or paid from the proceeds at closing, so ask the code office what is outstanding. Selling as is to a cash buyer is a common way to handle it.
